question.text: Which of the following is NOT typically cited as a BENEFIT of a globally diversified equity portfolio?

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook lists the benefits of global diversification as diversification of country-specific risks, access to superior risk-adjusted returns, and the ability to engage in tactical allocation across geographies. Currency risk is identified as a cost - not a benefit - of investing across borders, since cross-border holdings are exposed to exchange-rate movements. The Trap: "Elimination of currency risk" inverts the relationship - global diversification introduces currency risk; it does not remove it. Note: Source - NISM-Series-XXI-B Portfolio Managers Certification Examination workbook (Sep 2025), pp. 323 and 327.
